items.title: Set-quotients from an idempotent: the fixed points of an idempotent retraction satisfy the universal property of the quotient

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.10.8 at source lines 1321-1338: if A is a set, r : A -> A is idempotent and (r x = r y) is equivalent to x `eqr` y, then the type of fixed points of r satisfies the universal property of the quotient of A by `eqr`. The statement is long and its proof (source lines 1340-1368) is a full quasi-inverse construction, not a corollary of the general quotient theory: the map q(x) := (r(x), i(x)) is built from a witness of idempotence (lines 1341-1342), the equivalence e/e' has to be written down explicitly (lines 1344-1350), and both round trips depend on separate facts, the first on the fixed-point equation p : r(x) = x together with A being a set (line 1356) and the second on B being a set to discard the coherence component plus the hypothesis s to replace g(r x) by g(x) (lines 1361-1367).
